title: Exertional heat stroke during a road race, 21-year-old man
provenance: Vignette written 2026-09-30 for the evaluation harness; expected answers extracted from the cited documents.

intake.complaint: Collapsed while running a 10 km race in the afternoon heat; confused and not making sense.
intake.history: Previously well. Had been running for about 90 minutes in hot weather.

triage.note: Both extractors: level 2. A: Level 2 comes from several cells. ENVIRONMENTAL complaint Level 2 column (p9, x~131): 'Heat Stroke Temp > 39' (41.0). Adult Vital Signs Level 2 column (p7, x~131): 'HR > 120' (138), 'Temp > 39' and 'GCS < 13' (12). Primary triage Level 2 column (p4, x~246): 'Confused, agitated, disoriented' and 'Tachycardia, Weak Pulses'. Level 1 is defensible via primary triage Shock State L1 'Severe Tachycardia' (p4, x~136), but MTS gives no HR threshold for 'severe'. The MOH Heat Related Illness guideline flowchart (p16) says to triage heat stroke to the red zone. SBP 94 is not < 90. B: Level 2 comes from several cells: ENVIRONMENTAL 'Heat Stroke Temp > 39' (x~131, p9); the vital-signs cells 'Temp > 39', 'GCS < 13' and 'HR > 120' (x~131, p7); and the Rapid Assessment cells 'Confused, agitated, disoriented' and 'Tachycardia, Weak Pulses' (x~246, p4). Level 1 is defensible if HR 138 with SBP 94 is read as the Shock State cell 'Severe Tachycardia' (x~136, p4). The MOH heat-illness guideline says 'Triage to red zone'.

adjudication.method: two independent extraction passes (A, B); agreed items scored

A: The MOH HRI guideline does not mention cold/ice-water immersion. I did not add it from non-KKM sources, since KKM describes the cooling methods to use.
Rhabdomyolysis fluid targets (urine output 200-300 ml/h) appear only in the non-KKM CHAMP/AAST references. KKM gives urine output > 0.5 ml/kg/h, so the KKM target is used.
Triage L1 vs L2: MTS has no HR threshold for 'Severe Tachycardia' (L1). The guideline's 'red zone' covers both L1 and L2 in Malaysian EDs.
The HRI guideline's two cooling end-points differ: 'below 39 C' (p13) vs 'approximately 38 C / do not overcorrect below 38 C' (p14, p16). Both are accepted in the regex.
B: Is HR 138 with SBP 94 'Severe Tachycardia' (MTS Level 1)? MTS gives no numeric threshold beyond HR > 120 for Level 2, so both levels are accepted.

The KKM heat-illness guideline gives a 0.2 °C/min cooling target and 'do not overcorrect to less than 38°C'. It does not name cold-water immersion. The non-KKM rhabdomyolysis references were not needed and were not used.
